config.latency_origin: INTENDED dispatch time from the arrival schedule (R1)
config.loop_model: OPEN — dispatch schedule is independent of responses
config.name: p4_system_share1.00_cache_on
config.prompt_prefix: You are a helpful assistant. Answer concisely.
config.prompt_source: SYNTHETIC token noise, not a dataset — stated, not implied
config.slo_definition: completed AND ttft_ms < slo_ttft_ms AND p95(itl within the request) < slo_itl_ms
config.ttft_definition: first SSE chunk with NON-EMPTY delta.content

cache_evictions.description: Named for its source. NOT the same quantity as a preemption, which also frees blocks — R16 is the reason these do not share a name.
cache_evictions.name: cache_evictions

cache_hit_rate.description: blocks_reused / blocks_required_at_prefill. Meaningless without the workload's prefix-sharing structure attached.
cache_hit_rate.name: cache_hit_rate

completed_rps.description: Completions per second REGARDLESS of SLO. Distinct from goodput_rps, and distinct from offered_load_rps which is a parameter. Reporting any of the three as another is the classic error.
completed_rps.name: completed_rps

dispatch_drift_ms.description: actual_send - intended_send. A HARNESS HEALTH metric: drift above threshold invalidates the run (R1). Published alongside every goodput curve.
dispatch_drift_ms.name: dispatch_drift_ms

e2e_ms.name: e2e_ms
e2e_ms.source: client wall clock from intended dispatch

goodput_rps.description: Requests/sec that MET the SLO. The headline metric — raw throughput is gameable in both directions.
goodput_rps.name: goodput_rps

inflight_requests.description: Sampled on a fixed interval. The stationarity evidence for R11: a steady-state window whose in-flight count trends is not steady state, and its p99 is a statement about the ramp, not the system.
inflight_requests.name: inflight_requests
inflight_requests.source: load generator sampling of dispatched-but-unfinished requests

inter_arrival_ms.description: Gaps in the PRECOMPUTED schedule, not observed sends. Published so a reader can confirm the arrival process was what it claimed to be — a seeding bug that collapses Poisson toward deterministic is a degenerate workload with no error message (R14).
inter_arrival_ms.name: inter_arrival_ms

itl_ms.description: Gap between consecutive non-empty content chunks. Per-request series; pooled across requests before computing percentiles.
itl_ms.name: itl_ms

offered_load_rps.description: A PARAMETER, not an outcome. Reporting this as achieved throughput is a classic error.
offered_load_rps.name: offered_load_rps

output_tok_s.description: OUTPUT tokens only. Prefill tokens are reported separately; a combined total can be inflated arbitrarily by lengthening prompts.
output_tok_s.name: output_tok_s

output_tokens_per_request.description: Counts chunks with NON-EMPTY content. Empty-content chunks (special tokens detokenized with skip_special_tokens) are counted separately and are not tokens for timing purposes (BENCHMARK_METHODOLOGY §2).
output_tokens_per_request.name: output_tokens_per_request
output_tokens_per_request.source: client SSE parse, non-empty delta.content only

partial_hit_depth_blocks.description: Methodology §7 asks for partial-hit depth explicitly: it is where block-boundary and copy-on-write bugs show up, and a block-granularity hit rate alone cannot distinguish a deep match from a shallow one.
partial_hit_depth_blocks.name: partial_hit_depth_blocks

shared_blocks.description: Blocks genuinely shared by more than one live sequence right now. A gauge, sampled at the end of the window, not a counter.
shared_blocks.name: shared_blocks

slo_attainment.description: Steady-window requests meeting the full SLO / steady-window requests issued. Failures include errors and timeouts — they are SLO misses, not missing data.
slo_attainment.name: slo_attainment

tpot_ms.description: (last content chunk - first content chunk) / (output tokens - 1), one scalar per request. Reported ALONGSIDE the ITL percentiles, never instead of them — a mean hides the tail that the SLO is about.
tpot_ms.name: tpot_ms

ttft_ms.description: Intended dispatch -> first SSE chunk with NON-EMPTY content. Measured from INTENDED dispatch, not actual send, to avoid coordinated omission (R1). An empty-content chunk is not a first token.
ttft_ms.name: ttft_ms
ttft_ms.source: client wall clock from intended dispatch

name: p4_system_share1.00_cache_on
notes: RUN INVALID — must not back a published number: Steady state NOT verified: In-flight count TRENDS across the window: this is not steady state. Either the run is above the knee (where steady state cannot exist) or the window is too short. Percentiles from it describe a ramp. Numbers from this window are labeled 'unsaturated-window measurement'.
OPEN LOOP: requests were dispatched on a precomputed schedule, never gated on a response. Concurrency was unbounded.

All latencies are measured from INTENDED dispatch time, so they INCLUDE any harness lateness. That is the conservative direction and the guard against coordinated omission (R1). The drift series is in this artifact so a reader can subtract it if they want to.
Steady-state window [20s, 80s); warmup and drain requests were issued and DISCARDED (R11).
NOT PUBLISHABLE: Working tree is dirty — the measured code is not any commit.
Prompts were rendered from generator TOKEN IDS one word per id; the server re-tokenizes them. Realized sharing above is the id-level ORACLE and is an upper bound on any measured hit rate.
publishable_blockers: Working tree is dirty — the measured code is not any commit.

realized.output_length_control: max_tokens set per request from the output distribution; suppress_eos=True. Model-determined output length would make the workload non-reproducible across configurations (§4).
realized.prompt_len_floored_note: Requests whose realized prompt is LONGER than the drawn length because a shared prefix had to fit inside it. Expected and near-total for `conversational`, where the drawn length is the new tokens of the turn.

sharing.definition: block_sharing_rate = leading block-aligned prefix blocks already present in an earlier request / total block-aligned prompt blocks. This is the infinite-cache ORACLE hit rate and an upper bound on any measured one.
